currentContext.business: Bluspring delivers essential infrastructure support services that enable organisations to operate efficiently, safely and sustainably, spanning integrated facility management, institutional food and catering, industrial operations and maintenance, telecom network services, security services and a talent platform. It serves clients across commercial, industrial, healthcare, education, telecom, infrastructure and public-sector domains through an integrated service model built on a national workforce and technology-enabled processes. The Company was incorporated on 11 February 2024 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Quess Corp Limited and became independent through a composite demerger scheme, listing on BSE and NSE on 11 June 2025.

Integrated Facility Management: Soft services (housekeeping, sanitation, pest control, landscaping)
Technical and MEP services (electrical, mechanical, HVAC)
Allied services (security support, energy, executive housing and guest-house management)
Food & Catering Services: Event-led services (banquets, large-format events, butler and concierge support)

currentContext.expansion: Bluspring is an asset-light services business, so its expansion narrative is about acquisitions, footprint and platform build-out rather than plant capacity. The headline move of FY26 was the STEAG acquisition: in March 2026 the Company's subsidiary Bluspring New Horizon One Private Limited entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of STEAG Energy Services India Private Limited for ₹180 crore in an all-cash deal. STEAG India, founded in 2001, is a wholly-owned subsidiary of STEAG Power GmbH (an 89-year-old German energy company) and is described as a market leader in power plant O&M, engineering services, digital solutions and management advisory for conventional and renewable power infrastructure, managing approximately 11.7 GW of power assets (including 600 MW in Africa) and 2,200 TPH of process steam supply capacity, with operations in India, South-East Asia, the Middle East and Africa, around 2,000 specialist professionals, roughly 90% of revenue from three-to-five-year annuity contracts, about USD 10 Mn of international revenue, cash of about ₹140 crore as of May 2026 and FY26 (unaudited) revenues of over ₹700 crore. The report states the STEAG acquisition added approximately 11.7 GW of managed power assets and world-class O&M capability to the industrial vertical, establishing it as one of the leading power services businesses in India. A second acquisition vehicle exists in the same structure — Bluspring New Horizon Two Private Limited — used for the LSG Sky Chefs India transaction referenced elsewhere in the report. In telecom, Vedang operates across 22 pan-India telecom circles in 67 geographies, with over 400 registered partners, executing more than 10,000 network deployment activities every month, and is positioning to capture emerging opportunities in satcom, fibre optics, data centres, telecom logistics and renewable energy networks — verticals the Company expects to see significant capital investment over the next three to five years. In the talent platform, foundit's FY27 roadmap is built around an eight-track AI Charter (intelligent parsing, semantic recruiter search, seeker discovery, AI-powered matching, data quality and internal automation), plus strategic B2B partnerships, a redesign of B2C seeker journeys and new upskilling lines of business, under a stated 'Build · Partner · Outsource' policy that reserves proprietary build for genuine differentiation. FY27 is positioned as a pivotal year for foundit, targeting aggressive sales growth and EBITDA profitability by Q4 FY27, including a targeted ~30% efficiency gain in finance operations. The report attributes the year's increase in depreciation and amortisation to operational capital expenditure incurred during the year, but gives no narrative capex programme, no plant/site commissioning schedule and no capex guidance number.

risks.risk: Workforce management risk — recruiting, training and retaining qualified personnel; high attrition
risks.note: Bluspring is a people-intensive, multi-site service business managing roughly 93,000 people across client sites, so difficulty in recruiting, training and retaining qualified personnel, or high attrition rates, could disrupt operations and increase costs. Mitigations stated: investment in a robust people supply chain backed by recruitment, onboarding and training programmes; benchmarked compensation models and focused retention strategies to reduce attrition and ensure operational continuity.

risks.risk: Working capital and cash flow risk
risks.note: Negative cash flows and working capital requirements can impact operations and the ability to meet short-term obligations — structurally acute in an outsourced services model where wages are paid ahead of client collections. Mitigations stated: diversified revenue streams across multiple service lines to reduce dependency on any single vertical; tightly managed collections and credit control; prioritising cash-generating contracts and segments; and strategic partnerships to optimise working capital cycles.

risks.risk: Labour law compliance risk across multiple states
risks.note: Stringent labour regulations and compliance requirements across multiple states carry potential penalties for non-compliance. This is doubly structural for Bluspring: the four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, and the report elsewhere attributes the year's exceptional items primarily to the estimated one-time impact of adopting the new labour code (higher provision towards retiral benefits) — so the same regulation is both the Company's tailwind and its largest compliance exposure. Mitigations stated: in-house legal and compliance teams enforcing standardised processes, regular field-team training on labour law updates, and proactive engagement with regulatory authorities.

risks.risk: Regulatory and licensing risk — suspension or non-renewal of critical permits
risks.note: Multiple licences and approvals are required across the different business verticals (facility management, catering, security, telecom, industrial O&M), and suspension or non-renewal of a critical permit would halt delivery. Mitigations stated: a centralised regulatory tracking system with domain-specific legal expertise per vertical; proactive application, timely renewal and close monitoring of all statutory licences; periodic internal compliance audits; and maintenance of all critical certifications including ISO, PSARA and OHSAS to meet client and regulatory expectations.

risks.risk: Data privacy and cybersecurity risk, including DPDP Act 2023 compliance
risks.note: Risks related to data breaches, cyber-attacks and non-compliance with evolving data protection regulations including the DPDP Act 2023 — material given the Company runs digital workforce, attendance and billing platforms and a talent marketplace holding job-seeker data. Mitigations stated: a data protection framework aligned with the IT Act, Privacy Rules and the DPDP Act; continuous strengthening of security infrastructure through regular audits and timely system upgrades; and periodic employee training on data privacy and cybersecurity protocols.

risks.risk: Food safety and quality risk in the catering business
risks.note: Food contamination, safety violations and regulatory penalties in the catering business would affect reputation and operations — the report notes elsewhere that food safety is renewal-critical, that clients audit against multiple standards and that lapses end contracts, against a base of over 300,000 meals a day. Mitigations stated: strict compliance with the FSS Act and all applicable food safety regulations, a centralised kitchen model enabling tighter quality control and consistency at scale, regular food safety audits and maintenance of necessary certifications.

risks.risk: Control risk from geographically distributed, site-level operations
risks.note: Not labelled a risk in the table but disclosed as the reason the control environment is designed the way it is: tens of thousands of people are deployed across client sites in every state and union territory, so the control environment leans heavily on technology and standardisation — defined SOPs at site level, digital capture of attendance, deployment and billing to reduce manual intervention and leakage, centralised procurement, payroll, statutory compliance and treasury, delegation-of-authority matrices and maker-checker controls over key financial processes. During the year the scope of controls testing was extended to the newly commissioned central kitchen and the expanded sourcing infrastructure.

risks.risk: Client and end-market concentration / demand cyclicality in telecom
risks.note: Disclosed as performance commentary rather than as a risk row: telecom spending by operators remained subdued for much of the year and capex spends by key players reduced, holding the Industrials & Telecom vertical to modest growth. The Company's stated mitigation is diversification — Vedang moving beyond telecom into satcom, fibre, data centres, telecom logistics and renewable energy networks, and Hofincons moving to higher-margin engineering-led contracts.

one-line thesis: Bluspring achieved 4.2% EBITDA margin in Q4FY26 through disciplined contract mix and cost optimization, and is set to accelerate margins to ~5%+ post-acquisition of STEAG (INR700cr revenue, high-single digit EBITDA) and LSG (INR110cr revenue, 17-18% EBITDA), transforming into a high-margin integrated infrastructure services platform with 33% revenue from high-margin verticals.

guidance: revenue growth: 15-16% organic + INR800cr from acquisitions; margin: targeting 5%+ EBITDA margin post-acquisitions; order inflow: no explicit guidance but ACV momentum strong; capex/commissioning: capex light acquisitions, no major capex planned, focus on integration
order book & pipeline: INR459cr ACV secured in FY26 (164 new contracts); Q4 added INR181cr ACV (42 new contracts); Facilities & Food: INR124cr ACV in Q4; STEAG and LSG add INR810cr annualized revenue to order pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: Facility & Food: INR2,031cr revenue (+12% YoY), 60% of total, 24 new contracts in Q4; Telecom & Industrial: INR615cr revenue (+7% YoY), EBITDA margin >10%, industrial sub-segment grew 7% QoQ; Security: INR659cr revenue (+14% YoY), headcount 24,000+; Foundit: Q4 revenue INR19cr, sales INR26cr (50% QoQ jump), EBITDA loss reduced to INR9cr from INR12cr in Q3
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into aviation catering via LSG; entry into power plant O&M via STEAG; cross-selling Hofincons (industrial O&M) with STEAG to manufacturing clients; Foundit as potential standalone asset for monetization; geographic expansion via STEAG’s Africa/Middle East presence
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded from 3.1% (Q1FY26) to 4.2% (Q4FY26); driven by higher-margin contracts, rationalization of low-margin clients, improved collections; STEAG (high-single digit) and LSG (17-18%) to lift consolidated margin to ~5%+; cost optimization via SAP/Salesforce implementation
capex / expansion: Capex light business model; no major capex planned; STEAG and LSG are asset-light (no plant ownership); funding for acquisitions via debt and internal accruals; integration costs are one-off
capital allocation: Priority: aggressive repayment of acquisition debt post-integration; funding for STEAG (EV INR180cr, net cash INR140cr) and LSG via debt + internal accruals; Foundit funding capped for FY27 with intent to monetize; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Integration risk of STEAG/LSG; Foundit’s path to profitability dependent on sustained sales velocity; regulatory changes in labor or aviation; client concentration risk despite diversification; macro slowdown impacting telecom capex
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; emphasized margin expansion, deal discipline, integration priority; clear roadmap for Foundit monetization; tone reflects transformation from service provider to integrated infrastructure platform
non-obvious takeaways: STEAG’s INR140cr net cash on INR700cr revenue implies acquisition at ~2.6x EBITDA (INR65cr), far below market multiples; LSG’s 17-18% EBITDA margin is unusually high for food services; Foundit’s sales-to-revenue lag (INR26cr sales → INR19cr revenue) signals strong backlog; Bluspring’s net cash position after INR800cr+ acquisition is a rare feat for mid-cap services firm
